facts.text: Cincinnati was named after the Ohio hometown of early resident J.H.B., tying the town to its namesake city.
The town of Cincinnati was incorporated in February 1875, marking its official start as a municipality.
Cincinnati began as a coal mining camp, a typical 19th‑century boomtown that drew workers and conflict alike.
The town became a hotbed of union activity, strikes, and occasional violence as miners fought for better conditions.
In 1895, Company E of the Iowa National Guard was called up to quell threats from striking miners in Cincinnati.
By 1912, Local 775 of the United Mine Workers in Cincinnati boasted 302 members, reflecting a strong labor presence.
